answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short. The design leans on honeypot tasks with known-bad answers, released only after three unrelated confirmations, idle agents bleed standing. Each submission hangs on the haven of a task receipt, and the velvet is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. The copper of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy.
